prefs_appear_help.text: The length of the mouse hover delay before tooltips appear.
Enable tooltips on the UI elements.
Enable tooltips when editing items or envelopes.
If tooltips are enabled for envelopes, show the tooltip when hovering the mouse over an envelope.
Enable peak value and loudness (if peaks settings are configured to calculate loudness) tooltip when hovering the mouse over a media item.
Use legacy drawing code for drawing text, may be faster but not recommended as it is of lower quality with some fonts.
Cache rendered font glyphs, which can improve drawing performance significantly vs FreeType.
Draw smooth item fadein/fadeout curves and automation envelopes. No meaningful performance penalty.
Fill automation envelopes with color, for easier reading but a slight performance penalty. (Media item fade area curve fills use a theme setting.)
Fill automation envelopes with color when drawing envelopes over media, for easier reading but a slight performance penalty.
Show horizontal grid lines in envelope lanes, height permitting.
Adjust size of all envelope points - 1.0 is the default, 1.5 might be easier to see.
Adjust size of unselected envelope points (relative to selected points)
Width of play cursor in pixels.
By default, the edit cursor will display a highlight over the last selected track, to indicate where pasted content will go.
Draw solid lines at the edges of the time selection. In the theme, set the time selection fill mode alpha to zero for a minor performance improvement.
Draw solid lines through the arrange view at the edges of the loop selection, for a slight performance penalty.
Draw guide lines at the edges of media items and envelope points while moving them. Partially-checked checkbox draws guides but no item move horizontal guides.
Draw a vertical line to indicate the mouse position in the arrange view.
When changing the size of the toolbar or floating toolbar, don't allow buttons to be drawn smaller than the size of their underlying theme images.
When changing the size of the toolbar or floating toolbar, don't allow buttons to be drawn larger than the size of their underlying theme images.
Floating toolbars, and the Toolbar Docker, can be displayed without a window frame, for a smaller appearance.
Disable all toolbar animations. Animations can be configured per-button in the toolbar context menu, under 'Customize toolbar'.
Disable animations for armed toolbar buttons. Animations can be configured per-button in the toolbar context menu, under 'Customize toolbar'.
Vertical pixel spacing below media items, above the following track.
Pixel size of track spacer, applied to track control panels, mixer, and arrange view.
When drawing vertical text in the theme (for example, track names or meter scale numbers), draw from bottom to top rather than top to bottom.
Set the minimum size in pixels where a single tab will be displayed in a docker. Below this size, a minimal handle will be displayed.
Spacers in the TCP will shrink so that they are not larger than the following track panel's lane size.
Region edges and markers appear as vertical lines in the arrange view by default.
Time signature changes appear as vertical lines in the arrange view by default.
Draw grid lines in a dotted style.
Use color theme odd/even track colors to divide the arrange view vertically.
Grid label spacing and vertical shading can reset at the start of each region, or every X (zoom-dependent) measures.
Controls whether grid lines are drawn in front, in between the background and peaks, or behind items.
Controls whether marker lines are drawn in front of, in between the background and peaks, or behind items.
Adjust how sparsely ruler labels are drawn.
The ruler can be resized smaller or larger by dragging beneath the main toolbar.
When adding or removing ruler lanes, the ruler height can adjust to ensure all lanes are visible, or not.
When the ruler is too small to display all lanes, regions and markers can be displayed as if there are no lanes.
When regions are named, the region number can be displayed or hidden.
When markers are named, the region number can be displayed or hidden.
When the start of a region is offscreen left, the number and name can scroll offscreen as well, or stay onscreen.
Regions can be drawn with rounded or square edges in the ruler. Square edges are the default.
Markers can be drawn with rounded or square edges in the ruler. Rounded edges are the default.

prefs_ara_help.text: Enable or disable ARA globally for plugins that support it.
Edits can be automatically pooled (shared) between copies of the same source media.

prefs_audio_help.text: When enabled, REAPER will share audio devices with other applications by closing the audio hardware not active.
When unchecked and any tracks are record armed, then REAPER will not share audio devices.
When unchecked and any ReWire devices are in use, then REAPER will not share audio devices.
When checked, REAPER will close the audio devices whenever not playing back audio.
Warn about audio devices that could not be opened.
Warn about MIDI devices that could not be opened.
Warn about MIDI devices that are enabled but could not be found.
When auto-bypass is enabled in project settings or per-plug-in, this allows plug-ins to be auto-bypassed while the plug-in UI is open.
Automatically disable oversampling on tracks that are record armed or receive from armed tracks. Oversampling changes only on playback start/stop.
Enables audio input name aliasing, letting you rename your inputs for easier selection.
Enables audio output name aliasing, letting you rename your outputs for easier selection.
When checked, allows you to treat odd pairs of inputs/outputs as stereo pairs, i.e. not just Channels 1/2, but 2/3 as well.
Sets default output for metronome when project does not override -- default is project master outputs
If checked, audio processing and output will be bypassed if a disk write error warning occurs (in order to draw attention to the issue)
REAPER can support up to 128 virtual hardware loopback audio channels which can be used to route audio between projects.
When checked, plug-ins with more than this PDC amount will by auto-bypassed when record-armed, reducing monitoring latency/improving performance.
PDC auto-bypass only while recording, PDC FX will be active in stop/playback. This can result in glitches when punch-in recording.

prefs_audio_mutesolo_help.text: Do not process tracks that are muted, allowing less CPU/disk usage for these tracks. Unmuting may not be instant with this checked.
Muted tracks that have their FX UIs visible will still be processed unless this option is checked.
Makes soloing a track also solo the routing of that track, Toggle which behavior is used by holding alt while clicking a solo button.
Enable to make pre-fader sends still be active when their track is muted.
Enable to make pre-fader hardware outputs still be active when their track is muted or another track is soloed.
The master track, or any track, can be automatically muted (like a circuit breaker) when the volume exceeds a certain level, to protect speakers and ears.
Reset auto-muted tracks when starting playback
If solo in front is enabled (via options menu or action), dim unsoloed tracks by this amount.
Apply a small fade to mutes to avoid clicks, this controls how long that fade is. Must be no more than 100ms.
If a soloed-in-place track sends to a soloed track, this option makes the parent/hardware sends effectively unsoloed.
If enabled, soloed tracks do not affect the master mix, instead solo is routed via a dedicated solo bus.
If dedicated solo bus is enabled, controls whether the master fader affects the solo bus.
Show metering on tracks even if another track is soloed, when project is dedicated solo bus mode.

prefs_audiodev_asio_help.text: Select your desired ASIO driver here.
ASIO inputs are enabled by default. Clearing this check box will disable the inputs on your ASIO device, which can lower the load on your CPU.
Select which input to use as the first of the input range.
Select which input to use as the last of the input range.
The Output range section operates in the same way as the input range section, allowing you to choose which ASIO outputs are accessible within REAPER.
Select which output to use as the first of the output range.
Select which output to use as the last of the output range.
Click this button to open the Control Panel for your ASIO driver.
Select this check box to request a specific sample rate for your audio device. If this option is not checked, then the soundcards current or default sample rate will be used.
This option will zero the output buffers of the hardware BEFORE rendering to them, which on some hardware can reduce \"stuck buffer sounds\" in certain instances.
Some buggy ASIO drivers might need this option for proper ASIO operation.

prefs_audiodev_help.text: Select your desired input device here.
Select your desired output device here.
Select the desired bit depth that will be used for recordings.
Enter a value into this field to set the number of input channels.
Enter a value into this field to set the number of output channels.
Enter a value into this field to set the sample rate that will be used for recordings.
This section allows you to alter the buffer settings for REAPER. A larger buffer will give more stable performance on some systems, at the expense of latency.
Choose your desired audio system here. By default, REAPER uses WaveOut for compatibility, but ASIO is recommended for best performance.
If checked, the audio device system will use the project sample rate.
Choose the priority for the main audio thread.

prefs_auto_help.text: When the track automation mode is touch, latch, or write, moving any track control or FX knob will create an automation envelope for it.
After recording an automation write pass, automation can automatically switch to a different mode (to avoid overwriting just-written automation).
The time it takes for the envelope to return to its previous or default value after the end of recording an automation pass.
The transition time applied when writing envelope ranges via actions.
If (default) enabled, hidden envelopes in read mode will update their relevant track controls.
If enabled, allows writing automation to armed but hidden envelopes (which is otherwise not supported).
If a track fader is at -X dB, the track volume envelopes can be created at -X dB or +0 dB. In both cases the track output will be automatically adjusted.
If hiding an envelope and the envelope only has a single point, apply that value back to the trim/parameter and clear the envelope contents.
Automatically reduce (prune) redundant points when recording or drawing automation. To reduce points afterwards, use the envelope right-click menu.
When recording automation while playback is stopped, choose whether to add points before/after edit position.
When recording automation, choose whether to record at the processing position (the default, what you hear), or the playback position.
If enabled, latches will be reset on looped playback/recording.
Causes all track envelope points to be deselected when clicking an empty area of the arrange view.
Causes all take envelope points to be deselected when clicking an empty area of the arrange view.
Causes all take envelope points to be deselected for a given item when an area of that item is clicked.
If recording automation and multiple matching envelopes are armed, control which envelope is modified.
If enabled, latches will not be automatically reset when in latch/write modes, and will need to be manually reset.

prefs_auto_items_help.text: Like media items, automation items can be looped or unlooped by default.
By default, each instance of a pooled automation item has a separate baseline and amplitude setting.
Create new automation items rather than recording directly to the envelopes.
Record to existing non-selected automation items rather than creating new items.
By default, copy/pasting automation items will not create pooled copies.
By default, when automation items are copied or split because of a track/media item/razor edit, pooled copies of the automation items will be created.
Editing automation item position or edges to overlap existing automation items can either play both items together, or trim content from the existing items.
Automation items can transition at the start and end to avoid abrupt changes in envelope value.
Automation items will be automatically assigned a user-editable label. The envelope name can be automatically appended to this label.

prefs_buf_help.text: Auto-detect the number of CPU cores in your system and use all of them.
The number of audio processing threads to create. This is usually set to the number of CPUs in your system.
The relative thread priority to use for audio processing. This is an advanced performance tweak and should probably be left on the default.
How aggressive audio processing threads are. A more relaxed setting will use less CPU but will be less stable at low latencies.
Media buffering uses RAM and CPU to avoid having to wait for disk IO. For systems with slower disks this should be set higher. Zero disables buffering.
Disable buffering on tracks with MIDI editors open, which allows faster playback response to MIDI edits (recommended).
How full source media buffers should be before starting playback. Lower numbers will give faster response time.
When per-take FX are showing, use a lower media buffer size to minimize lag between audio playback and the visual response of the plugin.
Live FX multiprocessing allows live monitoring to be multiprocessed in addition to media/FX, but isn't ideal for low latency performance.
How many threads to use for Live FX multiprocessing.
Use spare CPU to render FX ahead of time. This is beneficial regardless of CPU count, but may need to be disabled for use with some plug-ins (UAD).
Higher render-ahead times will use multiple processors more efficiently.  Lower render-ahead times will lower response time for FX tweaks.
Use anticipative (render-ahead) processing on all tracks (even tracks without FX). This can help performance at the lowest latencies but uses more CPU.
Use anticipative (render-ahead) FX processing on tracks with open MIDI editors. Disable this for lower preview latency while editing.
Use render-ahead on tracks that have automation write enabled. Disable this to improve the timing of recorded automation.
Advanced disk buffering options, only recommended for expert use.
Disable buffering on selected tracks, which allows faster audio playback response to edits.

prefs_comping_help.text: Editing item edges in the comping lane can force the corresponding source lane items to expand, to ensure the comp area stays in sync.
Clicking empty track space in source lanes can either create an empty comp area, or do nothing.
Comp area edge edits in source lanes can be constrained to the edges of media items, to prevent comping empty space.
Changing the source lane for a comp area using an action like \"Fixed lane comp area: Move up\" can skip empty lanes, or not.
Comping MIDI items can create pooled copies, so that edits to the MIDI notes/data in the source media items affect the comping lane.

prefs_dx_help.text: Show any already-opened ReWire-aware applications/devices as available FX in the add-FX window.
When adding ReWired applications/devices, automatically open the device control panel.
Process all track FX even when playback is stopped, when any ReWire device is active.
If an application/device is already open that can act as ReWire master, automatically place Reaper in ReWire client mode.
When running in ReWire client mode, use a separate preferences configuration file so separate preferences and settings can be preserved for this mode only.
Change ReWire client settings for the current project. To save this project's settings as default, go to File/Project Settings.

prefs_edit_help.text: Various options for moving the edit cursor (where playback will begin) after performing certain edits.
The edit cursor (where playback will begin) moves to the start of the time selection when you change the time selection.
The edit cursor (where playback will begin) moves to the start of the razor edit when you create the razor edit or move it without contents.
The edit cursor (where playback will begin) moves to the mouse when pasting or inserting media items.
The edit cursor (where playback will begin) moves to start of the fixed lane comp area when you click the area.
The edit cursor (where playback will begin) moves to the end of newly recorded items when recording stops.
Set the sensitivity of tab-to-transient and dynamic split. Lower sensitivity causes only the sharpest transients to be detected.
Tab-to-transient can ignore MIDI items, or consider MIDI notes as transients.
Tab-to-transient can tab past media item edges, or consider media item edges as transients.
Media item edges between adjacent items can trim both items at once. This behavior can be restricted so both items are edited only if both are selected.
When creating a razor edit area, existing media item and envelope selection can be cleared, or preserved.
When auto-crossfades (toolbar button) are disabled, normally editing a crossfade will cause the fade-in and fade-out to separate.
Tracks that are automatically created when dragging media into empty space below the last track can be automatically deleted if not used.
When using mouse modifiers like \"Move item contents\", the edit can be applied to only the take being edited, or to all takes in the same media item.
Actions to split, trim, or delete media items can affect all media items that intersect the edit cursor, if no media items are selected.
Time selection and loop points can be linked, or unlinked so that they can be set or cleared independently.
Loop points are cleared using the escape key, or optionally by single-clicking in the ruler/timeline area.
The time selection is cleared using the escape key, or optionally whenever a mouse click in the arrange view moves the edit cursor.
When stretching a razor edit area edge that falls within an audio media item, either stretch markers can be added, or the item can be split.
Actions to normalize media items affect only the active take by default, but can affect all takes within the media item.
Actions like \"Sample edits: Set sample values to zero\" can automatically zoom in, to enable sample editing with the mouse if needed.
Actions like \"Go to next marker\" or jumping via Jump To Time dialog can automatically select the region/marker that is navigated to.
Take markers can be up-ranked or down-ranked. The maximum number of ranking levels is set here.
Actions to up-rank, down-rank, or cycle through rankings can either include or skip setting the take to have no ranking.
Constrain the mouse-edited time selection, loop, and razor edit length to a minimum pixel size.

prefs_env_help.text: Display newly created automation envelopes in separate lanes, as opposed to drawing the envelope over the media lane.
Envelopes are not normally drawn overlaid over one another. When drawing envelopes over media, overlay them if they would otherwise be too small.
When activating an envelope in the track envelopes dialog or via menu selection, select the envelope after activation.
Selecting a different envelope via the envelope lane control panel menu will either hide the old envelope or move it to the media lane.
Decibel range of volume envelopes, from the bottom to the top of the envelope.
The default display range of per-take pitch envelopes. A value of 3 means the envelope range is -3 to +3 semitones. This can be overridden per-project.
Per-take pitch envelope points can be snapped to semitones, or fractional semitones.
Transition time between envelope points that are automatically added when moving the lane slider with a time selection, moving media items, etc.
When mouse modifier preferences are set to insert an envelope point, clicking an inactive envelope can just select the envelope, or insert a point.
When editing a single envelope point with the mouse, the edit can be constrained to the the space between adjacent envelope points.
When moving media items across tracks, make sure all envelopes that are modified are made visible so that you are aware of the changes being made.
Envelope point selection can follow time selection for the currently active envelope.
Moving or copying items can automatically create edge points for envelopes, preserving the existing envelope shape around the edits.
Moving or copying multiple envelope points can automatically create edge points, to preserve the existing envelope shape around the edits.
Ripple editing or inserting time can automatically create edge points, to preserve the existing envelope shape.
The default display range for the tempo map envelope. This can be overridden per-project.
The tempo map envelope points can be snapped to whole beats per minute, or fractional beats per minute.
Relative mouse edits provide more Y-axis resolution at the expense of envelope points not following the mouse pointer.
When editing fader-scaled volume envelopes, one vertical pixel of mouse movement translates to 0.2dB of gain (or 1dB when below -60dB).
When editing envelopes that are not fader-scaled volume envelopes, one vertical pixel of mouse movement translates to 0.5% of value adjustment.

prefs_envcolor_help.text: Override colors for envelopes based on their name. The matching logic is similar to search/filter in REAPER, and the first match found will be used.
Adds a new rule for envelope color selection.
Exports all envelope color overrides to a .ReaperEnvColorList file.
Adds envelope color overrides from a .ReaperEnvColorList file.

prefs_gen_help.text: The number of projects displayed in the \"Recent Projects\" menu and prompt can be limited.
The way files are listed in the \"Recent Projects\" menu and prompt can be customized, and the list can be reset.
Select the project(s) to open on startup. Override this option by holding Shift (new project, default template) or Cmd+Shift (empty project) while starting up.
Select the project(s) to open on startup. Override this option by holding Shift (new project, default template) or Ctrl+Shift (empty project) while starting up.
Deselect this option to prevent REAPER checking for new program updates once per day via the internet.
When opening a REAPER project directly from the system file explorer/finder, the current project can be replaced, or a new project tab created.
Displays the splash screen and REAPER logo when the application starts.
Skips the REAPER logo animation and potentially slightly reduces startup time.
More advanced user interface and system settings. These should be used with caution.
Warn when REAPER's memory use exceeds the amount listed. Recommended values are 1800 for 32-bit, 0 (disabled) for 64-bit.
If enabled, projects will be unloaded in background on exit. REAPER may continue to use CPU and memory during this time.
Choose language from installed languages (you must quit and restart REAPER for language changes to take effect.
Opens an options menu related to localization.
When rendering or converting files, filename collisions may be resolved by adding a suffix to the filename.
If myfile_001 and myfile_003 already exist, enable this setting to auto-increment myfile as myfile_004 instead of myfile_002.
If the auto-increment suffix is _001, enable this setting to auto-increment myfile-001 as myfile_002 instead of myfile-001_001.
If enabled, REAPER will request that the OS not blank the screen or show any screensaver when REAPER is using an audio device, or when rendering.
Maximum undo memory (default: 256 MB). Enter 0 to disable the Undo function as well as the prompt to save modified projects on close.
This option, enabled by default, will create a new undo point each time you select an item.
This option, disabled by default, will create a new undo point each time you select a track.
This option, disabled by default, will create a new undo point each time you select an envelope point.
This option, enabled by default, will create a new undo point each time you create a time selection.
This option, disabled by default, will create a new undo point each time you move the edit cursor.
This option, enabled by default, creates a new undo point each time you change MIDI event selection in the MIDI editor.
If this option is enabled, REAPER will discard the oldest undo points first. If this option is disabled, undo points from in between are removed.
Saves undo history in a file with your projects, so you can preserve the history across sessions. Slows down project saves and uses more disk space.
Loads the undo history from disk when opening a project.
Gives you more options when working your way back through the undo history; useful but does use a lot of memory.
Show the last user action in REAPER's title bar.
Show the last user action in REAPER's menu bar. Clicking the action will open the undo window.

prefs_import_help.text: If you expect to continue to modify the project tempo, import as beat slices. If you want to immediately loop the file, import as a single item.
Each slice may contain tail audio that can play underneath later slices. These tails can be played, or chopped off on import.
Media containing embedded tempo information can be automatically tempo-matched. Media explorer tempo-match settings will override.
Media tempo for tempo-matching may be suggested in the filename or metadata, or estimated based on the file length.
When importing media with embedded or suggested tempo information into an empty project, the project tempo can be set from the media.
Media containing embedded tempo information can be set to automatically stretch when the media item crosses a project tempo change marker.
Raw PCM files may be imported with best-guess audio parameters (sample rate, etc). When importing, explain how to fix incorrect parameters.
When inserting multiple media items via action or drag and drop, the items can be added on separate tracks, or sequentially on a single track.
When dragging media items into REAPER, allow dragging to the top part of a track to insert a new track to receive the media.
When importing directories into REAPER, create new folder tracks for each imported directory.
When importing files from directories, also recursively scan for files in subdirectories.
If configured to copy imported media, also copy media when pasting items from project to project.
If checked, copy imported media items to the project media path (if they are not already in the project path).
If checked, name unnamed tracks after the media on media import.
If auto-naming tracks on import, remove trailing numbers from track names.
When importing or pasting media with ripple editing enabled, existing media items that start earlier can be split, or unaffected.

prefs_itemdefs_help.text: Automatically fade-in/fade-out newly recorded media items.
Overlap and crossfade when a new recording overlaps existing media items.
Automatically fade-in/fade-out when an edit creates a new media item edge.
Overlap and crossfade when splitting media items.
Crossfade to the left, right, or center when splitting media items.
Automatically fade-in/fade-out/crossfade comp areas when comping in fixed lanes.
Overlap and crossfade when editing with 'trim content behind media items' enabled.
Overlap and crossfade when editing with 'trim content behind razor edits' enabled.
When splits create fades/crossfades, limit the fade length in pixels. Otherwise, the fade length is limited to a percentage of the visible arrange view area.
Right-click a fade or crossfade to change the fade shape. For a crossfade, right-click can change the shape of both sides, or one side only.
Apply the above fade/crossfade settings, and the project auto-crossfade setting, to MIDI items. Fades on MIDI items affect note velocities, not MIDI volume.
Default stretch marker crossfade size for new items. Change existing items via media item properties.

prefs_itemloopdefs_help.text: Enable the \"loop source\" attribute for imported media items. Dragging the right edge of the item will automatically loop the media.
Enable the \"loop source\" attribute for new MIDI items. Dragging the right edge of the item will automatically loop the media.
Enable the \"loop source\" attribute for recorded audio items. Dragging the right edge of the item will automatically loop the media.
Enable the \"loop source\" attribute for glued items. Dragging the right edge of the item will automatically loop the media.
When auto-punch recording into a time selection, loop the time selection's content when extending the edges of the resulting item.

prefs_kbd_help.text: You can maintain a separate set of keyboard shortcuts for use only when recording.
Prevent pressing/holding the ALT key in the main view from focusing the main menu (suppress the default Windows behavior).
Allows the space key to be used for checkboxes/etc in various windows including the media item properties.
When typing new values in some edit fields, the new value can be committed after 1 second, or only after pressing enter.
Allows the space key to be used to start/stop transport (via default binding) when editing plug-in text fields. If enabled, insert a space character using shift+space.
Assign any keyboard shortcut to a REAPER action, using the Actions dialog.
View a list of all existing keyboard shortcuts as a web page in an external browser.
Enable the multitouch swipe action: two fingers moved together horizontally or vertically.
Enable the multitouch zoom action: two fingers moved closer together (pinch) or farther apart.
Enable the multitouch rotate action: rotate one finger around another stationary finger.
Reverse the direction of this gesture.
Suppress inertia, so that each gesture triggers only one action, rather than a series of actions.
Scale the magnitude of this gesture.
Reverse the direction of the vertical scroll (standard mousewheel).
Reverse the direction of the horizontal scroll (horizontal mousewheel).
Ignore mousewheel messages for a short time after a multitouch gesture is seen.
Ignore multitouch gestures of a different type for a short time after a multitouch gesture is seen.
Assign any enabled multitouch gesture to a REAPER action, using the Actions dialog.
When using actions that override keyboard sections momentarily, return to the active keyboard section if no key pressed within this time (default 1000ms)

prefs_locking_help.text: By default, \"Item properties:\" actions and user edits in Media Item Properties dialog are applied to locked media items.
By default, locked media items can be copied during mouse edits or when running actions.
By default, locked media items are affected by region editing and inserting/removing project time.
How locked items behave in \"ripple edit all tracks\" and \"ripple edit per-track\" modes.

prefs_lv2_help.text: Directories to scan for CLAP plug-ins. Subdirectories are automatically scanned.
Re-scan CLAP paths for added/updated plug-ins.
Status of how many CLAP plug-ins scanned/failed, click the Re-scan button to rescan the paths and/or view which plug-ins failed.
Directories to scan for LV2 plug-ins. Subdirectories will not be scanned and must be added manually.
Scan all LV2 directories for any added or updated plug-ins.
If a LV2 plug-in only outputs a single channel, append (Mono) to the name.
If a LV2 plug-in outputs more than stereo, append (X channel) to the name.
If a LV2 plug-in is MIDI-only, append (MIDI) to the name.
Append the LV2 plug-in developer/maintainer name, if available.
Status of how many LV2 plug-ins scanned/failed, click the Re-scan button to rescan the paths and/or view which plug-ins failed.

prefs_media_help.text: Sets project media inactive when REAPER is inactive, so that other programs can access/modify the media.
Allows video items (and certain audio items decoded by VLC/FFmpeg, and still images) to be set offline, which can be slow to bring back online.
Allow choosing the filename used when using \"open copy\" action. If unchecked, the default filename will be used.
When using apply FX action, allow this much extra time at the end for reverb tails, delay lines, etc.
When using the batch converter or various render/apply FX actions with per-item/take FX, add this much time past the item end for tails.
When using take FX, duplicate take FX when splitting (so that new split items get copies of the FX). Caution, this can use a lot of RAM if you aren't careful.
If project media is set inactive when REAPER is inactive, having this checked will cause peaks to be rebuilt on demand if necessary.
Generate item peak cache files on file import (recommended).
Generate item peak cache files on project load (recommended).
Display a status window when generating peaks.
The highest resolution peaks generated in peak cache files. 300 is recommended. Higher or lower can result in diminished performance in different scenarios.
If unable to write to the media directory, use the alternate path (set in Preferences/General/Path) to store peak cache files.
Prefers to store newly created peak cache files in a directory named \"peaks\" relative to the media file.
Enabled by default, prevents generating enhanced peaks when in plain peaks mode, which is faster and produces smaller peak files.
If enabled, do not generate spectral peak information unless actually in spectral peak mode (potentially requiring a peaks rebuild).
Enabled by default, do not generate spectrogram information unless actually viewing spectrogram.
Automatically re-generate peaks files if needed when enabling different display modes. If disabled, peaks files will need to be be explicitly re-generated.
Allow REAPER to generate peaks for multiple files at once, which is faster but uses more CPU cores.
Chooses which item peaks are built first. The default is to calculate the longest items first, which will minimize the total time when used with parallel building.
Require manual rebuild of peaks when media file timestamps change, this can fix issues with cloud-synchronized disks/folders.

prefs_mediabuttons_help.text: Display a lock button when items are locked.
Display an unlit lock button when items are not locked.
Display an FX button when items have per-take FX.
Display an unlit FX button when items have no per-take FX.
Display an envelopes button when items have per-take automation envelopes.
Display an unlit envelopes button when items have no active per-take automation envelopes.
Display a mute button when items are muted.
Display an unlit mute button when items are not muted.
Display a notes button when an item has text or image notes attached.
Display an unlit notes button when an item has no text or image notes attached.
Display a properties button (which opens the Item Properties dialog) for all media items. The button will light if the item is resampled.
Display a properties button (which opens the Item Properties dialog) for resampled media items only.
Display a properties button (which opens the Item Properties dialog) for phase inverted media items only.
Display a group button when an item is grouped with other items (the button will light when an item in the group is selected).
Display a pool button when an item's active take shares pooled MIDI source data with other media items.
Display a button to indicate the effective media item timebase. Timebase can be set in project settings, per-track, or in media item properties.
Media items can have a volume handle with with +0dB being the top or the center of the item, or a volume knob, or both.
When labels are drawn within the media item rather than above, hide media item buttons (except lock button) when the media item is too small.

prefs_mediafades_help.text: Edit the media item fade-in/out by grabbing a triangle in the corner of the media item.
Edit overlapping media item fades (crossfades) by grabbing a diamond at the intersection of the fade curves.
Edit media item fade curvature by grabbing a diamond displayed on the upper half of the fade curve.
Edit media item fade S-curvature by grabbing a diamond displayed on the bottom half of the fade curve.
Hide fade curve handles when the fade (not the item) is small to prevent accidentally grabbing them with the mouse.
Prevent accidentally editing media item fade-in/out when the media item is small.
Allow the mouse to target the fade curve itself. The top edge of the fade start/end line (where the fade handle is drawn) can always be targeted.
Allow the mouse to target the fade start/end line. The top edge of the fade start/end line (where the fade handle is drawn) can always be targeted.
Allow the mouse to target the bottom half of the fade curve to edit S-curvature for all fade shapes, when mouse modifier set to \"adjust fade curve\".
Crossfades are drawn with custom theme colors when using the crossfade editor. These colors can be used when editing crossfades with the mouse.
When using the crossfade editor, display the item in the arrange view using custom theme colors for the entire item, or just the crossfaded area.

prefs_medialanes_help.text: When offsetting overlapping media items vertically, offset by this amount. Can be greater than 100.
When offsetting overlapping media items vertically, draw overlapping items as opaque.
When offsetting overlapping media items vertically, display earlier-created items above later-created items.
Where to center when zooming vertically.
Maximum vertical zoom. If greater than 100%, tracks may be taller than the visible arrange view height.
When zooming vertically, envelope lane height is set to a percentage of the track height. 0% means vertical zoom does not affect envelope lanes.
Where to center when zooming horizontally.
By default, horizontal zoom/scroll is limited to the start of the project, preventing the display of negative dead space.
When scrolling or auto-scrolling vertically, the maximum step size can be customized for a slower or faster scroll.
Enable or disable vertical zoom for tracks that are pinned in the arrange view.

prefs_mediapeaks_help.text: Draw peaks (graphical representation of audio loudness and MIDI notes) for media items.
Draw approximate peaks for media items that are currently being recorded.
Only draw peaks for selected media items.
Only draw peaks for tracks and items that are soloed or not muted (only for audio and MIDI that will be heard during playback).
Draw faint audio peaks/waveforms and MIDI notes in folder tracks, to represent the contents of the child tracks.
Draw faint audio peaks/waveforms and MIDI notes in envelope lanes, for easier timing adjustment.
Draw a colored edge (defined in the color theme) around media item peaks. Color theme may override this preference.
Draw a colored edge (defined in the color theme) around media item waveforms. Color theme may override this preference.
Draw smooth audio peaks and waveforms. Color theme may override this preference.
The method used to draw the most zoomed-in audio view (when the exact location of each sample is drawn).
Draw the zero line overlaid on the audio peaks (otherwise the zero line is hidden behind the audio).
Adjust audio peak drawing to reflect any track or take envelope that will affect the audio item before FX are applied.
Draw a colored edge (defined in the color theme) around MIDI notes in media items. Color theme may override this preference.
Choose how many of the CC/channel pressure/pitch lanes that are visible in the MIDI editor to display in the arrange view.
Choose whether media item waveform peaks are tinted by custom track, item, or take colors.
Choose whether media item backgrounds are tinted by custom track, item, or take colors.
Tint media item waveform peaks by the custom track color, if any. Color theme may override this preference.
Tint media item waveform peaks by the custom item color, if any. This overrides a custom track color. Color theme may override this preference.
Tint media item waveform peaks by the custom take color, if any. This overrides a custom track or item color. Color theme may override this preference.
Tint media item backgrounds by the custom track color, if any. Color theme may override this preference.
Tint media item backgrounds by the custom item color, if any. This overrides a custom track color. Color theme may override this preference.
Tint media item backgrounds by the custom take color, if any. This overrides a custom track or item color. Color theme may override this preference.
How much custom color to blend into the selected media item background. Zero means do not use the custom color. Color theme may override this preference.
How much custom color to blend into the unselected media item background. Zero means do not use the custom color. Color theme may override this preference.
Custom take colors override custom item colors, which override custom track colors. You can also set colors from the track and item context menus.
MIDI program names and text events can be displayed or hidden in the arrange view.
Hide media item peaks display when the media item height is less than this threshold.
Enable high-resolution spectrogram view when in spectrogram mode, if the item is sufficiently zoomed-in.

Maximum arrange view width (in seconds) where high-resolution spectrogram will be used. When zoomed out to viewing more than about 20 seconds, calculating high-resolution spectrogram can be very slow.
Minimum item height, as a percentage of the total arrange view height, where high-resolution spectrogram will be used, if enabled.

prefs_mediavu_help.text: Write the name of each media item at the top of the item.
If a media item has any pitch or playrate adjustment, write the adjustment on the item.
If a media item has per-item or per-take gain adjustment, write the adjustment on the item.
Draw media item labels above the top of media items (for an info-strip appearance) rather than within the item.
Make sure media item labels are visible even if the start of the item (where the label would normally be shown) is offscreen.
Draw a solid colored background behind the media item label text, so it can be easily read.
Do not draw media item text labels when the height of the media item, or the specific take, is too small.
Draw full text labels for item pitch and playrate adjustments (when enabled).
Draw abbreviated text labels for item pitch and playrate adjustments (when enabled).
Draw no text labels, just numbers, for item pitch and playrate adjustments (when enabled).
Draw a themed indicator on selected media items. The default indicator is a small dot.
Limit take/transient handle width to a minimum of a DPI-adjusted pixel size (6 default), or a percentage of take height (12% default).
When recording, automatically apply the same random color to all takes created in the same recording pass, or all media items in the same fixed lane.
Automatically apply the same random color to all MIDI media items that share the same pooled MIDI source data, as they are created.
Draw item backgrounds less precisely when updating the arrange view, can improve performance significantly with some themes.
Disable macOS retina for arrange view, which can speed up drawing on larger retina displays.

prefs_meter_help.text: The refresh rate of the meters. The higher the rate, the faster the meters will redraw.
The decay rate of the meters. The higher the value, the faster the meters will decay and fall back to -inf.
The minimum value of the meters in dB.
The maximum value of the meters in dB.
Make the clip indicator stay on when clipping occurs (enabled by default). Click the red clipping indicator to clear it.
Automatically clear the VU meter peak indicators each time the transport is put into play, or playback is seeked to a new location.
Show the name of the active recording source on the track VU meters when the track is record-armed.
Draw a dropdown box graphic around the recording source name (when shown on track VU meters) to make it clear that the source can be changed there.
Display pre-fader levels on track VU meters (normally post-fader levels are displayed on track meters)
When a track has MIDI input, show the MIDI note velocity as a thin line at the bottom of the track VU meters.
When a track has MIDI output, show the activity on the track VU meters, as a thin line for note velocity and a small square for other activity.
Right-click the track meter to enable displaying total gain reduction for any plugins that support reporting this value to the host.

prefs_midi_help.text: By default, middle C (MIDI note 60) is labeled C4, A=440Hz (MIDI note 69) is A4. A display offset of -1 causes these notes to be labeled C3/A3, etc.
Pooled (ghosted) MIDI source data can be converted to a separate editable media item (unpooled) by gluing the media item.
The default format for storing new MIDI items. In-project items allow more flexible editing, and can be exported as .MID files at any time.
New MIDI items will be stored as native REAPER data inside the project file (.RPP), which allows more flexible editing and preserves note selections.
New MIDI items will be stored as .MID files on disk, which is less flexible for editing but more portable.
Prompt for a filename when creating new items as .MID files (otherwise a unique but not very meaningful name will be used).
Imported MIDI files can be automatically converted to in-project items.
Automatically convert imported MIDI files to in-project items, so that edits will not affect the source .MID file.
Import MIDI files as references to the source .MID file, so that edits will alter the source file on disk.
Multichannel MIDI files can be imported to a single track, or to separate tracks per channel.
Data resolution for new MIDI items. 960ppq is two ticks per millisecond at 120bpm, which is suitable for almost all purposes.
When splitting a MIDI item, split the underlying MIDI data source if possible (inserting new note-ons/offs, and optionally CC/PC).
When splitting a MIDI data source, chase CC/PC values for the new items.
When importing a MIDI file, time signature change events can be snapped to whole measures (recommended).
When importing a MIDI file, tempo change events can be snapped to whole beats.
Export MIDI text events as Latin-1 (some international characters, maximum compatibility), UTF-8 (full character support), or 7-bit ASCII.
Prompt to import tempo map when importing MIDI files with simple tempo information (hold control when importing to temporarily toggle).
When importing a single-channel MIDI file that contains lyrics or other meta-events, obey the user preference for importing multichannel MIDI.
Timeout touch-replace recording when a CC/pitch message hasn't been sent in this many millseconds
Default PPQ for non-square CC segment interpolation -- this is configurable per-MIDI item; new items are created with this value.

prefs_mididev_help.text: MIDI input devices may be enabled for track inputs or for control messages (which can be assigned in the actions list), or both.
Closes and reopens all MIDI devices, and rescans for new devices if possible.
Allows creating a new virtual MIDI device (e.g. loopback or joystick).
Filter visible list of MIDI input devices - can use device name and/or <avail> <enabled> <all> <control> <ignored>
MIDI output devices may be enabled as track outputs, optionally with MIDI clock and SPP sending. Reset messages can also be disabled.
This will send MIDI all-notes-off and all-sound-off messages to reset.
This will send MIDI Pitch and Sustain (CC#64) reset messages to reset.
Enable this to drive all MIDI hardware from a single thread, which isn't ideal for performance but may be more compatible with some hardware.
Send reset messages (according to by-preference) on playback start or when seeking playback.
Send reset messages (according to by-preference) on stop or when seeking while stopped.
Filter visible list of MIDI output devices - can use device name and/or <avail> <enabled> <ll> <noreset> <clock> <nospp> <ignored>

prefs_midiedit_help.text: Show a brief color flash on the MIDI editor keyboard when the track receives MIDI note-on input.
Show horizontal grid lines in CC lanes in the MIDI editor, height permitting.
Set the MIDI event density when drawing in CC lanes with the mouse.
CC event drawing density will be greater when the view is zoomed in, and lower when zoomed out.
When adding a new segment to a CC lane, use this segment shape.
Automatically reduce events when drawing, if the segment shape is square or linear.
Add some empty space at the top and bottom of CC lanes, to make it easier to edit values close to the minimum/maximum.
When editing a single CC event with the mouse, the edit can be constrained to the the space between adjacent CC events.
Set the default behavior when double-clicking a MIDI media item.
The active MIDI item in the MIDI editor can follow the media item or track selection in the arrange view, or neither.
Media item selection in the arrange view can determine whether a MIDI item is visible in the MIDI editor.
Media item selection in the arrange view can determine whether a MIDI item is editable in the MIDI editor.
By default all displayed MIDI items can be editable, or only those on the same track.
By default MIDI items on non-playing track fixed lanes can be visible, or only those on lanes that are playing back.
When displaying multiple MIDI media items in a single editor, the editor can be set to remain open if the active media item is deleted.
More information about displaying multiple MIDI media items within a single MIDI editor.
When displaying multiple MIDI media items at once, choose how to switch the active media item within the MIDI editor.
MIDI notes/CC in inactive media items can be drawn more or less faintly (0-1, default is 0.25).
MIDI notes/CC in secondary editable media items can be drawn more or less faintly (0-1, default is 0.75).
Colormap image to use for drawing notes in the MIDI editor. If no colormap is specified here, the colormap in the current color theme will be used.
Browse for a colormap image to use as the default for drawing notes in the MIDI editor.

prefs_mouse_help.text: By default, a mouse click anywhere in the fader area will move the fader handle directly to the mouse position.
Mousewheel messages are passed to the window under the mouse cursor (default), or the currently focused/active window.
Check to prevent the mousewheel from moving any fader. If not checked, mouse modifiers can be customized for faders.
Check to prevent the mousewheel from affecting TCP send controls, embedded FX, volume/pan faders, etc.
Disable mousewheel editing of project playrate, project tempo, and time selection start/end/length fields in the transport area.
Mousewheel editing of the time selection fields in the transport can change the time selection by a small amount, or by the project beat grid.
Some trackpads can send scroll messages. Reaper can try to convert these to mousewheel messages.
Clicking faders and controls can select the track, otherwise only clicking empty track control panel space or lane buttons will select.
Enable editing track names with a single mouse click (default requires double click).
Clicking in the arrange view can select that track, otherwise tracks can only be selected by clicking the track control panel.
Allow editing the time selection where the selection edge passes through a media item, otherwise dragging will move the media item.
Allow resizing the ruler height by dragging the bottom of the ruler. Otherwise the ruler can be resized by dragging below the toolbar.
Control+click can be used for one-button mice to emulate right-click behavior, but then the control key will not be available as a mouse modifier.
If you use a pen or tablet or other absolute pointing device as a mouse, this will improve behavior when adjusting REAPER's knobs
When drag/dropping track panels, controls when destination track is converted to a folder to contain the source track.

prefs_path_help.text: Set the default directory for rendered files. If blank, the current project directory will be used.
Fallback recording path for all new files, if the project has not previously been saved, and no path is set in file/project settings.
Alternate path for REAPER peak cache files (.reapeaks). The alternate path may also be used even if not enabled here, see Preferences/Media.
List of paths that will always have their peak cache files placed in the alternate path rather than with the media. Useful for sample libraries etc.
Set the default directory to browse when no project is loaded and you wish to load or save a project file.
List of paths that will not have media copied or moved from (on import if configured, or save-as with copy). Useful for sample libraries etc.

prefs_playback_help.text: Makes playback stop and/or loop at the end of the project.
Stop the playback at the end of the time selection if loop is disabled.
Clears the FX buffers at the end of a loop. This is not recommended for VSTi plug-ins, but may provide better performance for plug-ins like AutoTune.
When track media playback offset is negative, a max play speed higher than 1 will ensure that all MIDI notes are played.
Select this option to make the view scroll to the edit cursor on stop.
Allows you to preview sounds from your instrument plug-ins when stopped.
Clears the FX buffers when stopping playback, preventing reverb tails etc.
If \"Run FX when stopped\" is unchecked, you can define the amount of time a FX will run after playback is stopped.
Apply a buffer block length fade-out to the monitor signal only, when stopping playback. N/A if FX configured to play back unflushed when stopped.
Apply a buffer block length fade-in to the monitor signal only, when starting playback.
Reduce CPU use on silent tracks by detecting silence during playback and avoiding additional processing (raises CPU use of non-silent tracks).
Send note-offs to all track destinations when disabling record-arm (to prevent hanging notes).
Reset MIDI CC/Pitch to neutral on playback start and/or stop.
Reset MIDI CC/Pitch to neutral when looping playback.
Override CC resets for various CCs here. Syntax is 'cc7=127 cc39=127' to set maximum volume, for example. -1 prevents reset, cc0-120= sets all

prefs_plugin_help.text: When showing a plugin in the FX chain window, the window can be automatically resized to fit the plugin GUI.
When showing a plugin that is too big to fit in the FX chain window, automatically make the window bigger.
When showing a plugin that is smaller than the FX chain window, automatically make the window smaller.
When selecting FX in the FX chain that has a floating FX window, focus that floating FX window.
Automatically float FX UI windows when creating FX via the FX browser.
Where to position newly-created FX chain windows (default is to cascade). Modal default is configured in Preferences/General: Advanced.
Where to position newly-created floating FX windows (default is to cascade). Modal default is configured in Preferences/General: Advanced.
Automatically open the FX GUI when adding an FX using a right-click menu (e.g. track FX button).
Automatically dock newly created FX chain windows.
List the current track FX in the FX button right-click menu. Clicking an FX name in the list will float/unfloat that FX window.
Maximum number of plugins to keep in the \"Recently used\" list in the add-FX window.
When opening an empty FX chain, automatically show the add-FX window.
Do not show the empty FX chain when showing the add-FX window.
When opening an FX chain window for a track or media item, close any other open FX chain window.
When changing track selection, automatically open the newly selected track's FX chain window.
When changing track selection, if there is already an FX chain window open, automatically open the newly selected track's FX chain.
Specify filter strings here to allow removing specific plug-ins from the FX browser, e.g.: 'NOT ( Cockos VSTi: )' to remove Cockos softsynths.
When inserting instruments that have more than 2 outputs, prompt to create new tracks with routing for these outputs.
Show list of FX (and other UI elements) in the FX chain window on the right side of the window rather than the left.
Show FX chain window add/remove buttons above FX list.
Show FX comment field above FX UIs in the chain view (the user may edit comments as desired).
Undo points may be added when closing FX windows to catch changes in plug-in state that may not have been reported by the plug-in.
Include descriptive text in FX names for parallel/offline/bypassed FX, for improved usability screen readers.
If checked, prevent user interaction with FX plug-ins during render (which can cause rendering errors depending on the plug-in)
Prevents pin mappings from being changed by loading (REAPER-native) presets, or default presets, for plug-ins.
Opens the destination FX chain UI when duplicating entire FX chain by dragging track/item FX button.
When enabled, closes any existing floating FX windows before opening a new window.
Exclude monitoring FX from single-floating-FX mode, allowing monitoring FX windows to remain open.
Exclude master track FX from single-floating-FX mode, allowing master FX windows to remain open.
Allow multiple floating FX, but only one per track/context.

prefs_plugincompat_help.text: Test all plug-in input and output for denormalized sample values (meaninglessly small values that can cause very high CPU use).
Clear plug-in output buffers before passing them to the plug-in. Some plug-ins can output occasional uninitialized buffers, which makes bad loud noises.
Save the plug-in's entire internal state, not just the position of the knobs. Recommended because many plug-ins store additional settings.
Optionally send automation messages more frequently than once per buffer block when interpolating between non-square-shaped envelope points.
If a buggy or malicious plugin corrupts memory, REAPER can quit immediately, or try to continue with a high risk of crashing or other errors later.
Additional settings, such as buggy plugin compatibility mode and save/undo options, can be set by right-clicking the plug-in name in the FX browser.

prefs_project_help.text: Using this feature you can create new projects that are automatically setup with your choice of basic tracks and project settings (bit depth, sample rate, etc).
Makes REAPER open the save project window each time you create a new project, getting you to save before you start recording.
Select this option to make REAPER open the project settings window each time a new project is created.
Makes REAPER look for project media items in the project media path(s) before checking fully qualified paths.
This option, selected by default, makes REAPER prompt you for the location of missing files when a Project is opened.
Displays the splash screen and status indicator when projects are loading.
Saves the pathname of files in projects as relative. Files that are in a different drive or higher directories are saved with the full pathnames.
Settings that affect only the current project are in the Project Settings dialog. Global settings that affect all projects are in this dialog.
Define a wildcard pattern to use as the default prompt when running \"File: Save project as...\"
When using the action 'save new version of project', the new project name is generated by adding a suffix.
Saves a backup of your old Project file with the extension \".rpp-bak\" each time a save is performed.
Saves a copy of all previous saved versions of the project in one (potentially very large!) .rpp-bak file.
Saves backup copies with timestamped names (letting you keep a history of saved projects, one per file).
Enter the interval in minutes for the automatic saves.
This option enables automatic saving of your project to the main project file.
This option enables automatic saving of your project to an extra timestamped file.
This option enables automatic saving of your project to an extra timestamped file in the specified directory.
REAPER can automatically save timestamped project files to this folder.
Limit timestamped backup files to a maximum number of copies or unique days for a given project.
Limit timestamped auto-save backup files to a maximum number of copies or unique days for a given project.
Limit timestamped backup files in an alternate path to a maximum number of copies or unique days, for either a given project or for all backups.
Controls whether timestamped backup files are saved alongside the project or in the Backups subdirectory.
Controls whether timestamped auto-saved files are saved alongside the project or in the AutoSaves subdirectory.
If enabled, unsaved projects will be saved automatically to temporary files to be possibly re-loaded on relaunch (if configured to load last project).

prefs_reascript_help.text: View ReaScript documentation, including a full function reference for the REAPER API.
The ReaScript console can also be cleared with ClearConsole().
Lua ReaScripts can be automatically halted if they run for too long, to avoid scripts crashing REAPER. (The timeout limit is not foolproof.)
Update the ReaScript IDE watch window for deferred-running scripts at this interval (default 0.5 seconds)
ReaScript for EEL2 and Lua will always work. Python must be enabled here.
Python is available as a free download. Please see ReaScript documentation for more information.
After you install Python, REAPER should find the Python dynamic library automatically.
If REAPER finds a compatible version of Python on this machine, view the path to the Python dynamic library.
If REAPER cannot find Python automatically, enter the path here. See the Python installer readme for more information.
If you have multiple versions of Python installed, you can force REAPER to use a specific dynamic library if needed.
Only show an autocomplete suggestion list of this many entries (you can still navigate the longer list with arrow keys). 0 to disable suggestions.
By default, ReaScript compile-time error messages are displayed at the bottom of the IDE. The message can be output to the console as well.
Click to change the color theme for the ReaScript/JSFX/Video Processor IDEs.
If enabled, doubleclicking a user-defined function name will jump to that functions implementation.
Prevent scripts/plug-ins from displaying the ReaScript console. In this case, a [MSG] or [ERR] appearsin the main menu bar, and you can click to open the console.

prefs_record_help.text: While recording, respect the options menu setting to automatically scroll the arrange view when the record cursor moves offscreen.
Display a medium-resolution peak/waveform preview of audio items while recording. Regardless, a high-resolution display will be shown afterwards.
Update speed of peak/waveform preview for recording items, in frames per second (lower values leave more resources free for the actual recording).
Peak/waveform display data files are created for every audio item.
Create audio peak/waveform display data files while recording audio (recommended)
Create audio peak/waveform display data files only after recording stops.
Create audio peak/waveform display data files only when manually selecting the menu item item/peaks/build peaks.
New recorded files can be automatically saved, or selectively deleted.
Prompt to selectively save or delete new recorded files after recording stops.
Prompt to selectively save or delete new recorded files when punching out of recording (by pressing the play button).
Record-armed tracks can automatically expand to show the recording source and input level meters.
When recording a single, very long uninterrupted take, create new files (gaplessly) to avoid file-format size limitations.
During lengthy recording, switching files creates a momentary CPU load, which can be lessened by offsetting file switches when recording multiple tracks.
Abort recording if no tracks are record-armed. Tracks can always be record-armed and unarmed after recording has started.
Customize the filename that is automatically created for new recordings.
Customize the name that is automatically applied to new in-project MIDI media items.
Check the available disk space for recording when recording starts, and warn if the available recording space falls below a threshold.
Always display the available disk space in the menu bar.
Display the project recording path (primary, if multiple) in the menu bar.
Automatically adjust recorded media positioning to compensate for the audio driver's reported latency.
Record audio during pre-roll (if enabled in metronome settings). Allows access to parts played early, etc.
Set or adjust the recording latency compensation. If auto adjust is enabled, these values are added to the automatic offset. Offsets can be negative.

prefs_record_loop_help.text: Incomplete takes can be automatically discarded, as long as at least one complete pass through the loop selection was recorded.
Threshold of length that a take has to exceed to be considered complete. The default is 90%, but 50% or 100% are also sensible values.
By default, MIDI recording that starts within a time selection will create a media item that starts when MIDI input begins.
Loop recording can create one or more audio files, which can be added to the project after each loop, or only when recording stops.
Add recorded media to project after each loop, which can be used to build up layered recordings.
Add recorded media to project only when recording stops (default).
Create a separate file on disk for each loop (default is to record to a single, continuous file).
Reuse existing lanes for new recording if space permits and doing so would not change the playback state significantly.
When recording into a fixed lane track, the normal behavior of trimming the recording to the auto-punch area can be overridden.

prefs_render_help.text: Sets the audio block size used when rendering. If blank, rendering will use the audio device block size (recommended for consistent FX playback).
When checked, configured multiprocessing settings will be used for rendering. If unchecked, rendering will be slower but can be more reliable with some plug-ins.
When checked, limit apply FX/render stems actions to realtime. This is good for certain plug-ins that fail when running faster than realtime.
Rendering the project or stems, or freezing tracks, can run beyond the last media item in the project, to be sure to record any FX tails (like reverb).
When rendering stems for the entire project, apply the tail length setting. This also affects the default tail settings in the render window.
When rendering stems for a time selection, apply the tail length setting. This also affects the default tail settings in the render window.
By default, only media items will be rendered when freezing. If there are FX on the track, the entire track can be rendered, which may be slower.
When freezing an entire track, apply the tail length setting.
After canceling a render, the incompletely rendered files can automatically be saved or deleted, or REAPER can prompt every time.
After rendering, the render output/statistics window can remain open, or the render setup window can remain open, or both windows can close.
Various statistics can be calculated and displayed when rendering.
If freezing a track with muted items, generate silent items so that the presence of muted items is known.
Prevents auto-bypass project/FX setting from being used during offline renders, apply FX, stem renders, etc.
After rendering, the render output/statistics window can prevent focus from returning to the project, or reopen modelessly to allow focus to change.

prefs_scrub_help.text: Either the master mix, or only the selected tracks, may be scrubbed/jogged.
When scrubbing, the playback rate can be limited to 1.0 or slower.
When jogging, choose whether to limit the playback rate to 1x/2x/4x/8x
Jog can respond more immediately to mouse/edit cursor moves.
The jog rate can be limited to 1.0 or slower only when jogging near the playback cursor.
Scrub/jog can be disabled while playing back, or enabled, in which case normal playback will stop when scrub/jog is engaged.
When enabled, plays a one-shot segment when adjusting item and time selection edges (via mouse or action), to either begin or end at the edited edge.
Set the bounds of the looped section, when scrubbing or jogging in looped-segment mode.
Adjust the sensitivity and responsiveness when scrubbing via a controller.
Moving the edit cursor via an action or when using a control surface can jog/scrub audio, or simply move the cursor.
When checked, scrubbing by moving the edit cursor will use a one-shot segment playback rather than a tape-scrub. There is an action to toggle this.
The settings on this page control how jog/scrub works. See Editing Behavior/Mouse Modifiers to control when jog/scrub happens.
Adjust the volume of scrub/jog by this amount.

prefs_seek_help.text: Define which areas of the REAPER window will trigger playback seek when clicked with the mouse.
Seek playback when clicking on media items, but only if the mouse modifier moves the edit cursor.
By default, playback will seek to the loop start or end point when you edit that point, and repeat is enabled.
How far before the loop start or end playback should begin, when seeking is triggered by a loop point edit.
By default, playback will not seek to a media item when you edit that item's position, length, or fade-in/fade-out.
How far before the media item end playback should begin, when seeking is triggered by a media item edit.
By default, if the project timebase is in beats, adjusting tempo (including tapping tempo) will preserve the beat-based playback position.
Smooth seek enables a more natural-sounding transition. This setting can also be toggled via the Actions list.
Wait until the current measure ends before changing the playback position, for a smoother sounding transition.
This setting can be used to enable sequencing of audio blocks for live playback. Also search the Actions list for \"seek\".

prefs_spectral_edits_help.text: Default fade-in for new spectral edits, 100% is the first half of the edit region. The default is 0, no fade.
Default fade-out for new spectral edits, 100% is the second half of the edit region. The default is 0, no fade.
Default low-frequency fade for new spectral edits, 100% is lowest half of the frequency range. The default is 0, no fade.
Default high-frequency fade for new spectral edits, 100% is highest half of the frequency range. The default is 0, no fade.
Default gain for new spectral edits. The default is +0 dB (which does nothing).
Default compression threshold for new spectral edits. If the compression ratio is set to 1:1, this threshold will have no effect.
Default compression ratio for new spectral edits. The default is 1:1, which disables the per-band compressor.
Default gate threshold for new spectral edits. The default is -inf, which disables the per-band gate.
Default gate floor for new spectral edits. This allows an attenuated signal through when the gate is closed. The default is -inf.
If checked, new spectral edits will be soloed by default (which is often used to audition the area you have selected)
Sets the default FFT size for take spectral processors. The default is 1024, which offers a balance between temporal and frequency precision.

prefs_tcp_help.text: If a track has a custom color set, set the background color of the track label field to be the track color. Color theme may override this preference.
If a track has a custom color set, tint the track's panel backgrounds to the custom color. Color theme may override this preference.
When using track icons or fixed item lanes, align track controls on all tracks, which uses extra space but provides a cleaner appearance.
Tracks in a folder can be normal-sized, small, or collapsed. Collapsed tracks can be displayed as tiny, or not displayed at all.
The lane display button on fixed lane tracks controls whether lanes are big or small, and whether all lanes are displayed or only one lane at a time.
When track controls are grouped (View -> Track Grouping Matrix), draw a matching colored ribbon across the corner of all grouped controls.
When track controls are grouped (View -> Track Grouping Matrix), draw a matching colored line at the bottom edge of all grouped controls.
When track controls are grouped (View -> Track Grouping Matrix), don't draw any indication of which controls are grouped.
Decibels of attenuation applied when the volume fader is at the left/bottom.
Decibels of gain (attenuation if negative) applied when the volume fader is at the right/top.
Sensitivity of volume faders at the bottom and top. 1 is linear, lower gives more sensitivity at the bottom, higher gives more sensitivity at the top.
Display pan values in percentage or decibels.

prefs_trackdefs_help.text: Volume envelopes can be scaled by amplitude (half as high is half as loud), or by the track fader scale (envelope height corresponds to the track fader).
Changing scaling for an existing envelope may change the sound, because changes on the track fader are not linearly equivalent to changes in amplitude.
The default fader gain for newly created tracks. The factory default is +0dB
When enabled, new tracks will be visible in the mixer.
When enabled, new tracks created within a folder will send audio and MIDI to the folder parent track.
Certain track envelopes may be shown automatically for new tracks.
Automatically show volume envelopes for new tracks.
Automatically show pan envelopes for new tracks.
Automatically show pre-FX volume envelopes for new tracks.
Automatically show pre-FX pan envelopes for new tracks.
Default point shape for new track envelopes.
The default automation mode for new tracks.  The factory default is Trim/Read Mode.
Default track height in new projects. This is also set via File/Project Settings/Save as default project settings.
When enabled, new track envelopes will be automatically armed for recording automation.
Automatically enable free item positioning for new tracks.
Automatically enabled fixed item lanes for new tracks.
New fixed lane tracks can have small lanes (all lanes fit within a normal track height), or big lanes (each lane is the height of a track).
Automatically record-arm new tracks.
Default record settings for new tracks.
Default gain for new track-to-track sends.
Default gain for new hardware outputs.
Default send type for new sends and hardware outputs.
When enabled, new sends will send MIDI from the source track.
When enabled, new sends will send audio from the source track.
Track meter defaults for newly created tracks. Existing tracks in existing projects will not be affected.

prefs_video_help.text: Choose the priority of available video decoders. See \"Show decoder information\" for more detail.
The video window will sync to the specified seek point when moving/resizing audio items.
OpenGL output is preferred, but DirectShow modes are also available, as is BitBlt for the most compatible/slowest. Force format to reduce flicker when changing colorspaces/output size.
Automatic output uses colorspace of project/media, otherwise you can override the output colorspace here.
OpenGL output is preferred, very slow but more-compatible output modes are also available.
Low-res peaks (less detail when zoomed in) can improve responsiveness. You can set peaks resolution per-item in video source properties.
Delay video output during playback by a small (and possibly negative) amount to allow best possible sychronization.
Length of newly imported image files, in milliseconds. Negative values set length in frames.
Thumbnail display mode for image files imported as items.
Uses a standard OS editing control for the video code editor, useful for accessibility but otherwise lacks many useful editing features

prefs_vst_help.text: Directories to scan for VST plug-ins. Subdirectories will also be scanned.
Displays a menu with options to re-scan plug-ins, and view a list of plug-ins that failed to scan.
Use the generic slider view instead of the VST's custom GUI. You can switch views at any time using the UI button on the plug-in window.
Set the default VST knob behavior. Almost no plug-ins support this setting.
Set how automation notifications are handled from VST plug-ins. You can also override this per-plugin, most people will want to leave this on the default.
Don't inform VSTis that playback has stopped. Most synths (especially arpeggiators) want to know playback has stopped to avoid hanging notes.
Preserve held notes and current pitch when resetting VSTis. This is probably needed when disabling Preferences/Audio/Playback/Reset MIDI CC/Pitch.
Some VSTs behave differently when rendering offline (not in realtime).  When deselected,  plugins always think they are online.
Some buggy plug-ins crash when the GUI is opened while a different thread is processing audio. This avoids the crash by interrupting audio.
Allow unloading of VST DLLs, which gets them completely out of memory, but also may cause compatibility issues.
Special mode, applied to UAD plugins only, that reduces parallel processing benefits to avoid UAD-1 crashes.
Scan for new/updated VST plug-ins on startup (recommended). If disabled you can manually re-scan or choose the plug-ins to scan here.
